evidence: app/src/routes/index.ts:35-43 — stub return during build prevents live API calls in Gracile's build-time handler pass, which SPEC.md forbids ('don't fetch API data at build time')

justification.rationale: The sentinel guard buys something no stable API can (Gracile invokes GET handlers at build time with a stub URL, and the app must not hit the API then); it is an untyped magic string though, and the rest of the app deliberately uses the boring, documented surface.

findings.issue: Every handler route guards on the magic string url.hostname === 'gracile-static', an undocumented internal sentinel of @gracile/engine's build render pass (packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts constructs the stub URL with that hostname); it appears in no user docs or starters and can change silently between minor releases.
findings.suggestion: Centralize it: one exported helper (e.g. isBuildProbe(url) in src/lib/) with a comment citing the engine source, so a change only touches one module; raise it upstream for a documented build-time detection mechanism.

findings.issue: Templates consume handler results via context.props.GET as any casts (also at pokemon/[name].ts:223,231, types/[name].ts:44,52, moves/[name].ts:50,58, abilities/[name].ts:41,49); the {GET: ...} props-wrapping convention is only semi-documented (docs examples show it, runtime wraps in request-pipeline.ts), and the casts discard defineRoute's inferred typing.
findings.suggestion: Drop the as any casts and let defineRoute's type inference carry props through; if types mismatch, type the template context once instead of casting at each use site.

findings.issue: The whole framework is pre-1.0 and its docs state the project 'is in an alpha state' (gracile.js.org/docs/); the app also rides recently-stable Vite 8 (^8.3.5, stable 2026-03-12).
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact pin of @gracile/gracile (good as-is) and note in the README that upgrades are deliberate, since Gracile is alpha and minor releases can carry breaking changes; Vite 8 is fine — it's in the engine's peer range (^7 || ^8).

findings.issue: Relies on the framework's special-casing of a routes/404.ts entry (engine names it 404.html), a convention documented only via starters, not the 'Defining routes' docs page.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable — it matches the official starter pattern; consider a comment pointing at the convention for future maintainers.

summary: The app is deliberately conservative: it uses only the documented core of Gracile's current stable release (0.11.0, pinned exactly), mirrors the official Express starter for the server adapter, and avoids every genuinely experimental add-on in the Gracile ecosystem. The single reach past the documented surface is the internal 'gracile-static' build-time sentinel, repeated in all six route handlers — justified because it's the only way to keep the build from fetching live API data, which the spec forbids. Main improvement: centralize that sentinel behind one named helper so the framework coupling has a single point of failure.
